abstract: Segmenting neuronal somas in 3D brain images obtained through techniques such as tissue clearing and Light Sheet Fluorescence Microscopy promises to advance our understanding of healthy brains and the pathophysiological roots of neurological diseases. However, manual segmentation methods are often costly and time-consuming. Automating the segmentation through deep neural networks shows promise, but requires labeled ground-truth data that is also labor-intensive and expensive to obtain. To address these limitations, this work provides a platform within the open-source 3D image analysis software Vaa3D to efficiently and precisely label and automatically segment neuronal somas. A binary image of segmented somas is generated using a region-growing algorithm applied on 3D somas marked and bounded by a sphere around their center of mass, guided by a local Otsu threshold that can be manually overridden. The platform further supports principal component analysis of the segmented somas, allowing them to be rotated about their center of mass and aligned, in order for their characteristic shape to be captured in a probabilistic model. Finally, the platform supports the simulation of soma segmentation: it probabilistically reorients, repositions, and deforms segmented somas obtained from real data, generating synthetic ground truth data that can be used to train deep neural networks.
